params.body:
Two jobs in one pull request, because both touch `docs/bedrijfsregels/90-x-bevindingen.md`.

PR #342 conflicted with `origin/main` on exactly that file. The hand cannot update an existing branch, so its commit is cherry-picked here onto current `origin/main` and #342 can be closed.

---

## 1. The tools menu shows that it opens

*(This is the change from #342, unchanged apart from its finding number.)*

Shane reported two things on staging about the "Hulpmiddelen" button in the header of the own-stock list.

**The button gave no sign that it opens a menu.** Its two neighbours in the same header carry `dropdown-toggle`, `aria-haspopup` and `:aria-expanded`; this one was an icon and a word. It now has the same three, and the caret of all three buttons turns over while the panel is open, driven by `aria-expanded` so the affordance and what a screen reader hears cannot drift apart.

**The panel rendered badly on a narrow screen.** It carried `dropdown-menu dropdown-menu-right`, which pins it to the right edge of its button; on a phone that button is a third of a row wide, so the panel landed skewed and partly off-screen.

### What was chosen for the narrow layout, and why

Not left alignment and not the button's width: both keep the panel hanging off a small anchor, and both leave the same question open for the other two menus. On a phone the three header panels now become a **bottom sheet**, the pattern this application already uses for a menu on a phone: the `⋯` menu of a vehicle card became one in an earlier iteration. A sheet has no alignment to get wrong, it closes with a tap on the dim layer behind it (`@click.self`, as the row menu does), it carries the same Cancel row, and every line is a thumb-high target. It reuses the row menu's animations (`ui-sheet-op`, `ui-laag-in`), so the two sheets in the application look like one thing.

### The three header menus

They now agree: same `btn-group` wrapper, same `x-data="{ open: false }"`, same four ways to close (next to it, Escape, the choice itself, the sheet's backdrop), same plain `dropdown-menu` panel, same caret behaviour. The tools menu was the only one that differed; the other two only gained `@click.self` so the sheet's backdrop closes them too.

What the menu items do is untouched.

### Note, not in this change

`.ui-list-header` is styled only inside a `max-width: 767px` media block; there are no desktop rules for it, so the desktop header inherits the bought theme's button spacing. That is fine today but it means a header restyle has no place to live yet. Worth a section of its own when the next screen moves to Tailwind, and too large for a fix to one button.

Docs: rule **R P1-1.14** added in `docs/bedrijfsregels/31-p1-dagelijks-werk.md` (the header of the own-stock list), the defect recorded in `90-x-bevindingen.md` as **X-116** (it was X-112 in #342; X-112 was taken on `main` in the meantime), the tests tagged `@rule P1-1.14`.

---

## 2. Every finding keeps its own number

Four pull requests merged this evening each took the "next free" X-number without seeing each other, so `origin/main` carried **X-109, X-110 and X-111 twice each**:

```
$ grep -oE "^\| X-[0-9]+" docs/bedrijfsregels/90-x-bevindingen.md | sort | uniq -d
| X-109
| X-110
| X-111
```

The row that was merged **first** keeps its number; the later one moves to a free number at the end of the sequence. Merge order was #337 (20:55), #338 (21:10), #340 (21:26:11), #341 (21:26:33).

| Old | New | Finding | From |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| X-109 | X-109 (kept) | The buttons on the photo tab do what they say | #337 |
| X-109 | **X-113** | A select list in a modal opens at its own field | #340 |
| X-110 | X-110 (kept) | A relation has the same name everywhere | #338 |
| X-110 | **X-114** | The test suite runs on a cache that is empty per test | #341 |
| X-111 | X-111 (kept) | Picking a relation also fills the trade-in vehicles | #338 |
| X-111 | **X-115** | `odometerReading` is the mileage of the vehicle | #341 |
| — | **X-116** | The three menus in the own-stock header behave alike | this branch (#342) |

### Cross-references updated

Every reference to a renumbered finding, found by grepping the whole repository for the old numbers before and after:

- `docs/bedrijfsregels/14-s4-verkopen-aan-een-klant.md` (R S4-4.14): X-109 → X-113
- `tests/Feature/ModalDropdownAnchorTest.php` (docblock): X-109 → X-113
- `tests/Feature/RealGarantWireShapeTest.php` (comment at the cache line): X-110 → X-114
- `tests/Feature/CarpassWireShapeTest.php` (docblock): X-111 → X-115
- `tests/Feature/OwnStockHeaderMenusTest.php` (docblock, new file): X-112 → X-116

Untouched on purpose, because they point at the rows that keep their number: `tests/Feature/HandlerWiringTest.php` (X-109, #337), `tests/Feature/RelationDisplayNameTest.php` (X-110 and X-111, #338), `tests/Feature/BiddingBoxLabelTest.php` (X-112, the bidding-box labels row that was already on `main`).

No `@rule` tag changed: rule numbers were never duplicated, only finding numbers.

### Proof the sequence is sound

```
duplicates: (none)
rows:       116
range:      X-01 … X-116, 116 unique numbers, no gaps
```

(`X-01` … `X-09` are written zero-padded; the check normalises the padding before comparing against `seq 1 116`.)

---

## Not built here: making the next collision loud

This is the **second** time today that parallel work collided on this file. The first was the generated documents, fixed by taking them out of git in #329. Duplicate finding numbers are the same failure in a file that has to stay in git, and today it was found by hand rather than by the suite.

A cheap wall, in the shape of `RulesCoverageTest`: a test that reads `90-x-bevindingen.md`, collects the leading `X-<n>` of every row, and fails when a number appears twice — with the repeated number and both row titles in the message, so the author of the second branch sees at once which row to move. Optionally the same assertion for gaps, and for a reference to an `X-` number that does not exist in the table. It costs one file read and it turns a silent merge into a red CI run on the branch that arrives second.

Deliberately not in this pull request: the ask was these two jobs and nothing of my own.

## Verification

`php artisan test --filter='OwnStockList|OwnStockRowMarkup|StylesheetSyntax|AlpineExpression|RulesCoverage|RulesDocsBuild'` — **OK (26 tests, 667 assertions)**.
`--filter='OwnStockHeaderMenus|ModalDropdownAnchor|RealGarantWireShape|CarpassWireShape'` — **OK (24 tests, 141 assertions)**.

Run in a clean worktree on current `origin/main`, on a MySQL database built from `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` plus the post-2026-07-28 migrations, the way CI does.
params.title: The tools menu shows that it opens, and the duplicate finding numbers are resolved
